Aatrox.watch: Dodge Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade by watching the cast and moving outside its range or inside the blade’s edge so it does not hit you with the tip. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains hits you, leave the area immediately and use your saved Gnar E Hop to escape if needed. Aatrox R World Ender increases his healing and attack damage, so create distance and let it run out.
Aatrox.build: Build armor first against Aatrox’s main damage. If his healing prevents you from settling the fight during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce his healing. Counter Aatrox’s high armor with penetration or the max-health damage from Gnar W Hyper.
Aatrox.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip him with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before entering Aatrox’s counterattack range. Trade when Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance’s empowered attack has been used on a minion or Aatrox E Umbral Dash is on cooldown. When your Rage is full and you have an opening to engage, go in with Gnar E Hop as you transform, and finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Aatrox.laning: Even with full Rage, delay your abilities to control when you transform if the fight is in a bad spot, such as under the enemy turret. Pick a retreat position in advance for the period when Rage does not build after Mega Gnar ends.
Aatrox.combo: For Mini Gnar trades, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop onto a unit to bounce → basic attack, then keep hitting the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. For a transformation all-in, engage with Gnar E Hop at full Rage, land as Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a wall angle, position to throw the enemy toward the wall, stun them with Gnar R GNAR!, then follow with Gnar W Wallop.
Aatrox.escape: Right after you make Aatrox use E Umbral Dash is an opportunity to close the gap with Gnar E Hop or Gnar E Crunch. If you chain into Gnar R GNAR!, it is difficult for Aatrox to escape. If you need to dodge Aatrox W Infernal Chains, save Gnar E Hop for your escape instead of using it to engage.
Aatrox.phase: In the late game, choose terrain with wall angles to create opportunities for Mega Gnar to engage.
Aatrox.teamfight: Before a fight, choose terrain with a wall and position so you can throw the enemy toward it. Engage as Mega Gnar, stun them against the wall with Gnar R GNAR!, then continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. If you are still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.

Akali.watch: Prioritize dodging the first shuriken from Akali E Shuriken Flip. If it marks you, her second dash will follow even if you try to escape, so if it hits, do not use Gnar E Hop too early; create distance when she goes in. You cannot dodge the first dash of Akali R Perfect Execution by walking, and its second hit deals more damage based on your missing health.
Akali.build: Start with Null-Magic Mantle to survive the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Akali’s damage is mostly magic and Gnar has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Also build up your total health to prepare for the second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution.
Akali.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip her with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before Akali comes within range to counterattack. Keep hitting the same target to gain Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. If your Rage is full, hold your abilities until you have an opening to engage, then go in with Gnar E Hop and transform when Akali’s mobility ability is on cooldown.
Akali.laning: Do not force your way into Akali W Twilight Shroud; trade back when Akali comes out to attack you. Manage your trades so your Rage does not fill in an unwanted position, and finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Akali.combo: For short trades as Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop onto a unit to bounce → basic attack. For a transformation all-in, go in with Gnar E Hop at full Rage, land as Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a position to push Akali into a wall, stun her with Gnar R GNAR! and continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop.
Akali.phase: Gnar peaks in the mid game when his first core item is complete; in the late game, choose terrain with wall angles for fights.
Akali.teamfight: Before a fight, position so you can push Akali into a wall. If you are Mini Gnar, do not force an engage; build Rage by poking from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. After engaging as Mega Gnar, use Gnar R GNAR! toward the wall, then continue the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Akali.escape: Your opportunity to engage comes after you dodge Akali E Shuriken Flip’s first shuriken and Akali W Twilight Shroud is also down. If Akali R Perfect Execution is not back up yet, close the gap with Gnar E Hop, and if you have an angle to a wall, pin her with Gnar R GNAR! If only one of Akali’s mobility spells is down, she can escape with the other, so don’t rush your engage.

Aurora.watch: If Aurora Q Twofold Hex hits you, its return deals damage too, so move out of the straight line between Aurora and you. The return damage increases as health decreases, so if health is borderline, retreat before the curse returns. After Aurora R Between Worlds appears, leaving it slows you, so if you are in a dangerous position, get out before the area forms.
Aurora.build: Start with Null-Magic Mantle to survive the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Aurora’s main damage is magic and Gnar has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If Aurora P Spirit Abjuration’s healing prevents you from winning during Mega Gnar, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce her healing.
Aurora.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip her with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks, keeping attacks on the same target to use Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. If health has decreased while the curse from Aurora Q Twofold Hex is applied, do not extend the trade; retreat before it is recalled. When your Rage is full and you have an opening to engage, go in with Gnar E Hop as you transform and finish the fight during Mega Gnar.
Aurora.laning: Even with full Rage, hold your abilities to control when you transform if you do not have a good position to engage. Rage does not build for a while after Mega Gnar ends, so finish the trade before then and move to a safe position.
Aurora.combo: For short trades as Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop onto a unit to land and move forward → basic attack. Move along the boomerang’s return path so you can catch it, and keep hitting the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. For a transformation all-in, engage with Gnar E Hop at full Rage, land as Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Before using Gnar R GNAR!, position so you can throw Aurora into a wall.
Aurora.escape: Do not engage just because Aurora W Across the Veil is on cooldown; also check Aurora E The Weirding and Aurora R Between Worlds. If Aurora used a mobility ability to engage and Aurora R Between Worlds is not back up yet, you have an opportunity to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. Transform as you go in and push her into a wall with Gnar R GNAR! to make it difficult for Aurora to escape.
Aurora.phase: In the late game, choose terrain with wall angles for fights.
Aurora.teamfight: Choose terrain where you can use a wall ahead of time, then look for an angle to engage as Mega Gnar and push Aurora into the wall with Gnar R GNAR!. If you are still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage. Aurora W Across the Veil can be used again after a takedown, so do not leave a low-health ally behind when retreating.

Chogath.watch: Cho’Gath Q Rupture knocks you up after a warning appears beneath you, so move sideways when you see it and save Gnar E Hop for that moment. Cho’Gath W Feral Scream silences you and prevents you from using abilities, so avoid facing him directly; if it hits, walk away first. If your health is at or below half, retreat outside the range of Cho’Gath R Feast, which deals true damage.
Chogath.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Prioritize magic resistance against the magic damage from Cho’Gath Q Rupture, W Feral Scream, and E Vorpal Spikes. If Cho’Gath P Carnivore’s healing prevents you from winning during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce it.
Chogath.fight: As Mini Gnar, use ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw on the same target to gain Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. After dodging Cho’Gath Q Rupture or after Cho’Gath uses it on the wave, if your Rage is full, engage with Gnar E Hop as you transform. Finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Chogath.laning: Cho’Gath E Vorpal Spikes pierces in a straight line even through minions, so step aside from the direction Cho’Gath is facing when he basic attacks. Push the lane or pressure him early to limit his chances to build stacks, and manage your Rage so you do not transform in an unwanted position.
Chogath.combo: For Mini Gnar trades, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop onto a unit to bounce → basic attack. For a transformation all-in, approach with Gnar E Hop at full Rage and land as Mega Gnar. If you have an angle to push him into a wall, throw Cho’Gath into it with Gnar R GNAR!, then follow with Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss.
Chogath.escape: Cho’Gath has no mobility abilities, so when he uses Cho’Gath Q Rupture on the wave or immediately after you dodge it, you have an opportunity to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. Approach while avoiding the front of Cho’Gath W Feral Scream; if you are silenced, walk away instead of trying to use a mobility ability. Rage does not build for a while after Mega Gnar ends, so finish the fight before you transform back.
Chogath.phase: Cho’Gath gets stronger as he builds stacks, so in the late game fight from a position where you can use a wall.
Chogath.teamfight: Before a fight, choose terrain where you can use a wall and decide which way to push with Gnar R GNAR!. Engage as Mega Gnar, set up an angle to throw Cho’Gath into the wall, then continue the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you are still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.

DrMundo.watch: Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw hits the first target it contacts and deals damage based on current health, so be especially careful when your health is high and keep minions between you. Don’t stay in a long fight while taking empowered basic attacks from Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma. If Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active, account for its healing and movement speed increase and don’t spend time trying to secure a kill.
DrMundo.build: Build armor first to reduce the physical damage from Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma. If you can’t win within Mega Gnar’s duration because of the healing from Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases, Q Infected Bonesaw, and W Heart Zapper, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing.
DrMundo.fight: As Mini Gnar, whittle Dr. Mundo down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. Hit the same target repeatedly to use Gnar W Hyper’s percent max health damage and movement speed increase. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities if you don’t have a good angle to engage. Bait out Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases, then engage as you transform into Mega Gnar and finish the fight before the transformation ends.
DrMundo.laning: Dodge Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw by keeping minions between you. After a trade, if you can step on the canister Dr. Mundo drops, do so along your retreat path to deny its healing and passive cooldown reduction.
DrMundo.combo: At full Rage, use Gnar E Hop to bounce off a unit and approach, transforming midair and landing as Mega Gnar. First use Gnar W Wallop to trigger Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases’ first ignore-immobilizing effect, then use Gnar R GNAR! to knock him into a wall. Before using Gnar R GNAR!, position yourself so Gnar, Dr. Mundo, and the wall are in a straight line.
DrMundo.escape: Dr. Mundo has no ability to create distance on his own, so engage when Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is also down and Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw either misses or is blocked by a minion. Then close the gap with Gnar E Hop or E Crunch and catch him with Gnar R GNAR!.
DrMundo.phase: Gnar peaks in the mid game as his first core item is completed, so line up your Rage and a wall angle to fight. In the late game, fight in terrain with wall angles, and don’t spend time trying to kill Dr. Mundo while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active.
DrMundo.teamfight: Choose a fight location with a wall in advance and position so Dr. Mundo will be pushed toward it. As Mini Gnar, build Rage from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then engage in Mega form. Bait out Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases first, then use Gnar R GNAR! to knock him into a wall.

Fiora.watch: Fiora W Riposte blocks attacks and immobilizing effects, and can stun Gnar if it blocks a stun, so don’t rush Gnar R GNAR! while Riposte is available. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, hug a wall to block one side’s vital.
Fiora.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora E Bladework. If you can’t win within Mega Gnar’s duration because of Fiora’s healing, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce it.
Fiora.fight: As Mini Gnar, whittle Fiora down with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks. Hit the same target repeatedly to use Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. Close the gap right after Fiora uses Q Lunge, but bait out Fiora W Riposte before going in as Mega Gnar, and finish the fight before the transformation ends.
Fiora.laning: Stand on the opposite side from the exposed Vital and briefly counterattack when Fiora moves in toward it. Manage your Rage so you don’t transform in an unfavorable position.
Fiora.combo: At full Rage, if Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora W Riposte are down, close in with Gnar E Hop as you transform, then chain Gnar W Wallop stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Before using Gnar R GNAR!, position so you can knock her toward a wall; if the wall stun lands, follow with Gnar W Wallop.
Fiora.escape: Right after making Fiora use Q Lunge is your chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. If Fiora W Riposte is also down, continue the engage with Gnar R GNAR!; if Riposte is still available, don’t stun her first.
Fiora.teamfight: In terrain with a wall, confirm Fiora W Riposte is down, then engage as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR! to knock her into the wall. If you’re still Mini Gnar, build Rage from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, hug a wall to block one side’s vital.

Camille.watch: Camille E Hookshot travels along a wall and can engage from far away to stun you, so stand away from walls and watch for the moment her hook catches one. Use Gnar R GNAR! then if its forced movement can interrupt her leap. Don’t waste crowd control as Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum engages; if trapped, wait out its duration before counterattacking.
Camille.build: Build armor first against Camille’s main damage. However, armor won’t reduce the true damage from Camille Q Precision Protocol, and Camille W Tactical Sweep deals damage based on max health, so be wary of stacking only health. If you can’t win within Mega Gnar’s duration because of the healing from Camille W Tactical Sweep, buy Executioner’s Calling first.
Camille.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back out of Camille’s counterattack range. Avoid trading right after Camille P Adaptive Defenses activates its shield; fight once the shield has been removed. At full Rage, if you have a good angle to engage, go in with Gnar E Hop as you transform, but finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Camille.laning: Stand away from walls and among minions to avoid Camille E Hookshot’s wall route, and create distance before taking the empowered basic attack from Camille Q Precision Protocol. Even at full Rage, delay using abilities to control when you transform if you’re under a turret or in a position without backup.
Camille.combo: If Camille’s engage ability is down and you’re at full Rage, use Gnar E Hop to land on a unit and bounce off as you transform, then chain Gnar W Wallop stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you get a wall angle, position so the opponent is pushed into it, use Gnar R GNAR!, then continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. Throw Gnar Q Boulder Toss where you can pick it up again.
Camille.escape: When Camille E Hookshot is down, you have a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. If Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum is also down, use Gnar R GNAR! to lock her down and reduce her chance to escape. If only one of Camille’s mobility abilities is down, she can escape with the other, so check that both are down before engaging.
Camille.phase: Early on, Gnar has the advantage with ranged poke, so pressure Camille’s farming while she is weak before her first core item. In the late game, choose terrain where Gnar R GNAR! can knock her into a wall.
Camille.teamfight: Position so Camille is pushed toward the side with a wall behind her, then engage as Mega Gnar and look for a wall stun with Gnar R GNAR!. If you’re still Mini Gnar, build Rage from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and wait to engage until you transform. Don’t use Gnar’s crowd control as Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum engages; if trapped, wait out its duration before counterattacking.

Darius.watch: If Darius E Apprehend pulls you in, he can follow with basic attacks, Darius W Crippling Strike, and Darius Q Decimate, so poke from outside E range. When you see Darius Q Decimate, move outside the blade or hug him to reduce its damage and healing. If Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up, create distance to drop them; if you’re low on health with stacks, get completely out of Darius R Noxian Guillotine range.
Darius.build: If Darius Q Decimate’s healing makes it hard to win during Mega form, buy Executioner’s Calling first. Build armor against Darius’s main damage, but it won’t protect you from Darius E Apprehend’s armor penetration or the true damage from Darius R Noxian Guillotine. Against Darius’s high armor, use penetration or Gnar W Hyper’s percent max health damage.
Darius.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to gain Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed, then briefly back away. Once Darius E Apprehend is down, if you’re at full Rage, close in with Gnar E Hop as you transform into Mega Gnar and commit to the fight. End the fight if Darius P Hemorrhage has built up heavily or Mega Gnar is about to end.
Darius.laning: Poke right after Darius uses Q Decimate to clear minions, and catch Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to reduce its cooldown. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities if you don’t have a good angle to engage, so you don’t transform in an unfavorable position.
Darius.combo: As Mini Gnar, slow Darius with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, follow with basic attacks on the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back away. At full Rage with Darius E Apprehend down, bounce off a unit with Gnar E Hop as you transform, then chain Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you get a wall angle, use Gnar R GNAR! to knock him into the wall and stun him, then continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop.
Darius.escape: When Darius E Apprehend misses or is on cooldown, Gnar has a window to trade. If Darius E Apprehend is still available, save Gnar E Hop to respond to it.
Darius.phase: In the late game, choose fights in terrain where you can use walls.
Darius.teamfight: Before a fight, position in terrain with a wall. At full Rage, engage as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR! to knock the opponent into the wall. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw as you build Rage. If Darius P Hemorrhage has stacked and Darius R Noxian Guillotine kills you, its cooldown resets, so get out of range when your health is low.

Gangplank.watch: Gangplank E Powder Keg becomes more dangerous the longer it sits, so back away if there’s a primed keg nearby, and don’t stand on overlapping kegs. If you can directly destroy a keg from outside its blast radius, do so. Gangplank W Remove Scurvy removes crowd control and restores health, so check whether he has used it before going for a kill with Gnar R GNAR!.
Gangplank.build: Build armor early in lane to counter the physical damage from Gangplank Q Parrrley and Gangplank E Powder Keg. Gangplank P Trial by Fire and Gangplank R Cannon Barrage deal true damage that resistances can’t block, so consider health as well. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy makes it hard to finish the fight during Mega Gnar’s window, buy Executioner's Calling first.
Gangplank.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to use Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. Trade when Gangplank E Powder Keg has just been placed and isn’t primed yet, and back off if a primed keg is nearby. If your Rage is full and there’s an opening to engage, close in with Gnar E Hop as you transform, then finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Gangplank.laning: Choose your movement direction so you can catch Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and keep harassing and clearing the wave. Even at full Rage, delay your abilities to control when you transform if Gangplank E Powder Keg is primed or you’re under the enemy turret.
Gangplank.combo: For a short trade as Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, landing on a unit to move forward → basic attack. For an all-in during transformation, engage with Gnar E Hop at full Rage, transform into Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down and you have an angle to the wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to knock him into it and stun him, then follow with Gnar W Wallop.
Gangplank.escape: Gangplank has no ability to create distance on his own, so engage with Gnar E Hop after you destroy Gangplank E Powder Keg or just after he places one, before it’s primed. Once Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, he can’t remove the crowd control from Gnar R GNAR!, so look for a guaranteed kill then. Finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Gangplank.phase: Midgame, when your first core item is complete, is Gnar’s peak. In the late game, start fights in terrain with an angle to a wall.
Gangplank.teamfight: Take position in terrain where you can use a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR! to knock enemies into it. Before applying decisive crowd control to Gangplank, check whether Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down. If you’re still Mini Gnar, harass from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to build Rage, and account for whether Gangplank R Cannon Barrage has been used when timing objective fights.

Garen.watch: Garen Q Decisive Strike empowers his basic attack and silences you, preventing you from retaliating, so don’t engage first while it’s active. Garen E Judgment punishes you the longer you stay close, so move out of its spin range. Garen W Courage grants a shield and tenacity right after activation, so delay Gnar R GNAR! by half a beat. If your health is below half, beware Garen R Demacian Justice, which deals true damage based on your missing health; stay out of its range.
Garen.build: If Garen P Perseverance’s healing makes it hard to win during Mega Gnar’s transformation, buy Executioner's Calling first to reduce his healing. Prioritize armor against the physical damage from Garen Q Decisive Strike and Garen E Judgment. Garen R Demacian Justice deals true damage that resistances can’t reduce, so consider your total health as well.
Garen.fight: As Mini Gnar, focus Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks on the same target to use Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed, then back off before Garen can retaliate. Trade briefly after Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered attack is used. If your Rage is full and there’s an angle to engage, go in with Gnar E Hop as you transform, and finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Garen.laning: Garen has no mobility, so push the lane to expose him to ganks, then create a numbers advantage elsewhere after pushing past the lane. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities to control when you transform if you’re in a bad position, such as under the enemy turret.
Garen.combo: At full Rage, approach Garen with Gnar E Hop as you transform into Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you see Garen W Courage’s animation, delay Gnar R GNAR! by half a beat, and take position first so you can knock Garen into a wall. If you stun him against the wall, continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop.
Garen.escape: The moment right after Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered attack is used on a minion or otherwise fully spent is an opportunity to engage. If Garen activates Garen W Courage, wait for its initial shield and tenacity to wear off, then close the distance with Gnar E Hop / Crunch and look for Gnar R GNAR!. Garen has no ability to create distance on his own, but don’t engage if Mega Gnar is about to end or your health is below half.
Garen.phase: Garen W Courage’s growth stacks are permanent, so you’re at a disadvantage as time goes on. In the late game, look for fights in terrain with an angle to a wall.
Garen.teamfight: Choose terrain with a wall in advance and take a position that lets you knock Garen into it. Engage as Mega Gnar, stun him against the wall with Gnar R GNAR!, then continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, don’t force an engage; harass from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to build Rage.

Gwen.watch: The center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!’s cone deals true damage, so walk to the side to get out of the center. When Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, you can’t target her from outside the mist, so fight when it ends or when you can enter it. Keep your distance from Gwen R Needlework, which slows and deals damage based on your maximum health.
Gwen.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first early on, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Prioritize magic resistance against Gwen’s main damage, but dodge the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip! by positioning, since resistance can’t block its true damage. If her healing makes it hard to win during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner's Calling first to reduce it.
Gwen.fight: As Mini Gnar, focus Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks on the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then create distance when you gain movement speed. If your Rage is full immediately after baiting out Gwen E Skip 'n Slash, close in with Gnar E Hop and trigger your Mega Gnar transformation. Don’t stand in the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!, and finish the fight before your transformation ends.
Gwen.laning: Keep Gwen at a distance where she can’t basic attack to stop Gwen P A Thousand Cuts from healing her. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities if you don’t have a good place to engage, and control your damage in trades so you don’t waste your transformation under the enemy turret.
Gwen.combo: At full Rage, if Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is down, approach with Gnar E Hop as you transform. After landing, chain Gnar W Wallop’s stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Before finishing with Gnar R GNAR!, take position so you can throw Gwen into a wall.
Gwen.escape: Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is her only mobility ability, so right after she uses it is your chance to close the distance with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. In areas with many minions, Gwen E Skip 'n Slash can come back sooner, so engage from the side without minions. As Mega Gnar, hold her with Gnar W Wallop or Gnar R GNAR!.
Gwen.phase: In the late game, look for Mega Gnar fights in terrain where you can use a wall.
Gwen.teamfight: Before the fight, choose terrain with an angle to a wall and take position so you can throw Gwen toward it. Engage as Mega Gnar, make her hit the wall with Gnar R GNAR!, then extend the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, harass from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to build Rage.

Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain through low-health minions to close the distance, so back away when those minions are between you. Watch for the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet, and if you’re trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard's Edge’s perimeter, wait until the blades disappear.
Irelia.build: Prioritize armor against Irelia’s main damage. If healing from Irelia Q Bladesurge makes it hard to win during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner's Calling first to reduce it.
Irelia.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back off before entering counterattack range. When Irelia Q Bladesurge is down and your Rage is full, engage with Gnar E Hop as you transform and take a short fight.
Irelia.combo: At full Rage, use Gnar E Hop to land on an enemy or unit and bounce off as you transform, then follow Gnar W Wallop’s stun with a basic attack and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle to a wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to knock the enemy into it and continue the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Irelia.escape: Right after baiting out Irelia Q Bladesurge is your chance to engage with Gnar E Hop or Gnar E Crunch. Watch for the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet, and before engaging, check the cooldown of Gnar E Hop so you can escape after Mega Gnar ends.
Irelia.phase: In the late game, choose fights in terrain with an angle to a wall.
Irelia.teamfight: Irelia R Vanguard's Edge and Irelia E Flawless Duet have a major impact in teamfights, so prioritize targeting Irelia. If you’re still Mini Gnar, build Rage from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then take a wall angle as Mega Gnar and engage with Gnar R GNAR!.
Irelia.laning: Don’t leave a low-health minion between you and Irelia that she can dash to. Create distance as minions are about to die. Manage your Rage so you don’t transform in an unfavorable position.

Illaoi.watch: Dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit. If it hits, fight back if you can; otherwise, break the tether, dodge the first tentacle, then wait beside it for the mark to expire. When Illaoi R Leap of Faith is used, spread out and move away from areas covered by tentacles.
Illaoi.build: If Illaoi’s healing makes it hard to finish the fight during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling first. Build armor against the physical damage from Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God, Illaoi Q Tentacle Smash, and Illaoi W Harsh Lesson. Illaoi W Harsh Lesson deals damage based on your max health, so avoid stacking a lot of health alone.
Illaoi.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip her down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before entering Illaoi’s counterattack range. Keep hitting the same target to use Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. Right after Illaoi W Harsh Lesson, you may have a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop, but don’t fight for long where tentacles are set up.
Illaoi.laning: Keep the wave away from walls and last-hit outside Illaoi E Test of Spirit’s range. Taking damage builds your Rage, so manage your trades to avoid transforming under the enemy turret when you don’t want to.
Illaoi.combo: As Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, landing on a unit to bounce → basic attack for a short trade. Move along the boomerang’s return path to catch it, and keep hitting the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. If your Rage is full and Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is down, close in with Gnar E Hop, transform, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Line up a wall angle and finish with Gnar R GNAR!.
Illaoi.escape: Right after baiting out Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is your window to engage with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. Dodging Illaoi E Test of Spirit also lowers the risk of being caught. If Mega Gnar is about to end or Illaoi R Leap of Faith has been used, end the fight and leave the area covered by tentacles.
Illaoi.phase: In the late game, make the most of Mega Gnar where you have an angle to a wall, but don’t fight near walls covered by Illaoi’s tentacles.
Illaoi.teamfight: Destroy Illaoi’s tentacles when you can; if you can’t, draw her into open ground away from walls. While Illaoi R Leap of Faith is active, spread out and deny her a target to hit. As Mega Gnar, fight where no tentacles are set up, line up a wall angle, push her into the wall with Gnar R GNAR!, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.

Jax.watch: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and move out of its stun range. Jax Q Leap Strike can use minions as a springboard, so don’t stand close to your allied minion wave. Cut short extended trades before Jax P Relentless Assault builds his attack speed.
Jax.build: Jax’s basic attacks and attack speed are the core of his damage, so prioritize effects that reduce attack speed. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so consider both armor and magic resistance. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on your max health, so be careful about stacking a lot of health alone.
Jax.fight: As Mini Gnar, poke briefly with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, and stop basic attacking when Jax E Counter Strike is active. After Jax Q Leap Strike and Jax E Counter Strike are down, you have a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. If your Rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to engage and transform into Mega Gnar.
Jax.laning: Watch for allied minions Jax can use as a springboard for Jax Q Leap Strike, and pressure him while Jax E Counter Strike is down. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities to control when you transform if there’s no good angle to engage.
Jax.combo: If Jax Q Leap Strike and Jax E Counter Strike are down and your Rage is full, close in with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar. After landing, chain Gnar W Wallop’s stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a position to knock him into a wall, finish with Gnar R GNAR!.
Jax.escape: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, don’t use Gnar E Hop carelessly; save it to get out of stun range. Right after Jax Q Leap Strike and once Jax E Counter Strike ends, you can engage with Gnar E Hop. Finish the fight and fall back before Mega Gnar ends.
Jax.teamfight: When Jax engages with Jax E Counter Strike active, don’t group up nearby; avoid the area stun. As Mega Gnar, line up a position to knock the enemy into a wall, use Gnar R GNAR!, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.

Jayce.watch: When Jayce is holding his cannon and sets up Jayce E Acceleration Gate, Jayce Q Shock Blast may be coming, so immediately sidestep out of its line. When he holds his hammer, watch for Jayce Q To the Skies! engages and the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Jayce.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Jayce W Lightning Field and Jayce E Thundering Blow, but remember that it won’t block the physical damage from Jayce Q Shock Blast.
Jayce.fight: As Mini Gnar, poke the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks, then back off before entering counterattack range. If Jayce Q To the Skies! is down and your Rage is full, close in with Gnar E Hop, transform, and follow up with Mega Gnar’s stun.
Jayce.laning: Jayce Q Shock Blast travels in a straight line, so move side to side while farming and immediately dodge to the side when you see Jayce E Acceleration Gate. If you fall behind early, farm defensively instead of forcing a comeback. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities if there’s no good angle to engage so you don’t transform in a bad position.
Jayce.combo: With full Rage and Jayce Q To the Skies! down, approach by using Gnar E Hop to land on a unit and bounce, transforming as you do. Then stun with Gnar W Wallop, followed by a basic attack and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a position to knock him into a wall, stun him with Gnar R GNAR! and follow with Gnar W Wallop.
Jayce.escape: Right after Jayce Q To the Skies! is used is your window to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. In hammer form, also watch for the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow; engaging after it’s used reduces the risk of being pushed away.
Jayce.phase: In the late game, prepare to fight in terrain where you have an angle to a wall.
Jayce.teamfight: Bait out Jayce Q To the Skies!’s leap, then engage as Mega Gnar. Position yourself to knock him into a wall, stun him with Gnar R GNAR!, then chain your crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.

KSante.watch: If you’ve been hit by K'Sante Q Ntofo Strikes repeatedly, move out of range or save Gnar E Hop to avoid the pull and stun from the next Q. K'Sante W Path Maker grants unstoppable status and damage reduction while charging, so don’t use Gnar W Wallop; sidestep the dash instead. Don’t face off with your back to a wall, where K'Sante R All Out could push you through the terrain.
KSante.build: Account for K'Sante’s high armor by including penetration in your build, and make use of Gnar W Hyper’s damage based on max health. Armor is more useful than magic resistance against K'Sante’s main sources of damage. K'Sante W Path Maker’s true damage can’t be reduced by resistances, so consider health as well.
KSante.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to gain Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed, then get out of K'Sante’s counterattack range. Once K'Sante W Path Maker is down and you’ve confirmed his other mobility ability is also unavailable, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform if your Rage is full. When K'Sante R All Out is active, take advantage of his weakened state to focus damage, but don’t absorb it alone for long.
KSante.laning: K'Sante Q Ntofo Strikes stacks even when he hits minions, so check its status and keep enough distance to dodge the empowered next Q. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities if there’s no good angle to engage K'Sante; finish the fight and back off before your transformation ends.
KSante.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, landing on a unit to bounce → basic attack, and move in a direction that lets you catch the boomerang. For an all-in, build full Rage, close in with Gnar E Hop and transform, then chain Gnar W Wallop’s stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a wall angle, knock K'Sante into the wall with Gnar R GNAR! to stun him, then follow with Gnar W Wallop.
KSante.escape: If only one of K'Sante W Path Maker and K'Sante E Footwork is down, he can escape with the other, so don’t rush your engage. Once you’ve seen both mobility abilities used and K'Sante R All Out is still unavailable, you have a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. If K'Sante Q Ntofo Strikes’ empowered next attack is still available, first move out of range or save Gnar E Hop to dodge it.
KSante.teamfight: Before the fight, choose terrain where you have an angle to a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar and position yourself to knock K'Sante into the wall with Gnar R GNAR!. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage. Hold your crowd control while K'Sante W Path Maker is charging; while K'Sante R All Out is active, focus your team’s damage together and have a source of healing reduction.
KSante.phase: In the late game, fight in terrain that gives you an angle to pin enemies against a wall.

Kennen.watch: Kennen's P Mark of the Storm stuns after three stacks, so back off when you have two marks and wait for them to wear off. Kennen Q Thundering Shuriken hits only the first target, so stand behind minions. Spread out from allies when Kennen R Slicing Maelstrom has an angle to engage.
Kennen.build: Kennen deals mostly magic damage, and Gnar has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Survive the early game with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Kennen.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks, then back off before entering counterattack range.
Kennen.laning: Block Kennen Q Thundering Shuriken from behind minions, and position yourself to step out briefly only when last-hitting. Even at full Rage, hold off on transforming by delaying your abilities if there is no good opening to engage, and finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar wears off.
Kennen.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, bouncing off a unit to move forward → basic attack. For an all-in at full Rage, approach with Gnar E Hop and transform, then follow with Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle to a wall, position yourself and use Gnar R GNAR! to push them into it, then continue the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Kennen.escape: Kennen E Lightning Rush is his escape, so after he uses E to engage and spends it, look for your chance to go in. If you have two stacks of Kennen P Mark of the Storm, back off first and let them wear off, then close the gap with Gnar E Hop.
Kennen.phase: In the late game, choose terrain where you can get an angle to a wall before fighting.
Kennen.teamfight: Spread out so Kennen R Slicing Maelstrom does not hit several allies, and use vision to check where Kennen could engage. From terrain with an angle to a wall, engage as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR! to push enemies into the wall. If you are still Mini Gnar, harass from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.

Kayle.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Kayle deals mostly magic damage, and Gnar has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If Kayle W Celestial Blessing's healing keeps you from finishing the fight during Mega Gnar, buy Executioner's Calling first to reduce her healing.
Kayle.fight: Keep attacking the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then use the movement speed to get out of Kayle's retaliation range. If your Rage is full, hold your abilities until you get an opening to engage, then approach with Gnar E Hop and trigger Mega Gnar.
Kayle.laning: As Mini Gnar, harass with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, but back off before entering Kayle's retaliation range.
Kayle.combo: At full Rage, approach Kayle with Gnar E Hop and transform, then follow Gnar W Wallop's stun with basic attacks and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle to a wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to push Kayle into it and stun her, then continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. If Kayle R Divine Judgment is active, do not focus damage during her invulnerability; let the time run out with a stun, then attack again.
Kayle.escape: Kayle has no mobility ability to create distance on her own, so close the gap with Gnar E Hop when you get an opening to engage. Avoid the slow from Kayle Q Radiant Blast, and catch her with Gnar W Wallop's stun or Gnar R GNAR! toward a wall before she can escape with Kayle W Celestial Blessing.
Kayle.teamfight: Choose a route from the flank or outside vision that lets you reach Kayle directly, so she has no time to attack from the back line. Before engaging as Mega Gnar, line up Gnar R GNAR! between Kayle and a wall, and attack when your allies' crowd control comes in alongside yours. If you are still Mini Gnar, build Rage from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. During Kayle R Divine Judgment's invulnerability, lock her down with crowd control and save your damage until it ends.
Kayle.watch: Kayle Q Radiant Blast slows and reduces armor and magic resistance, so avoid taking a direct hit. If Kayle heals and gains movement speed with Kayle W Celestial Blessing, it uses up Gnar’s Mega Form duration, so when she’s close, stun her first with Gnar W Wallop. While Kayle R Divine Judgment is active, don’t unload your damage. Lock her down with crowd control and wait for the invulnerability to end.

Kled.build: Build armor first against the main damage from Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, W Violent Tendencies, and E Jousting. Armor cannot block the magic damage from Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!!. Since Kled W Violent Tendencies and R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! scale with maximum health, be careful about stacking a lot of health alone.
Kled.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks to trigger Gnar W Hyper, and do not stay in Kled's retaliation range for long. Dodge the pull from Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, then, once Kled E Jousting and R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! are on cooldown, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform if your Rage is full.
Kled.laning: Even at full Rage, delay your abilities to choose when to transform if there is no good opening to engage. If you cannot kill Kled after he dismounts, create distance so he cannot build Courage. If he stays in lane, pressure him so he cannot farm minions comfortably.
Kled.combo: At full Rage, use Gnar E Hop to bounce off Kled or a unit on landing and transform, then follow Gnar W Wallop's stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. To finish, position yourself so you can throw Kled into a wall, then use Gnar R GNAR!. If he is stunned by the wall, continue the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop.
Kled.escape: If Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope hits you, use Gnar E Hop to create distance before it pulls you in. To engage, look for a window when both Kled E Jousting and R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! are on cooldown. Then close the gap with Gnar E Hop / Crunch and follow with Gnar R GNAR!.
Kled.phase: Kled weakens after the laning phase and mid game, so do not give him an early lead. In the late game, fight in terrain where you can get an angle for Gnar R GNAR! into a wall.
Kled.teamfight: Use vision on your flanks to spot Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! approaching from a distance. If you can’t stop it, maintain your formation, bearing in mind that he charges at the first enemy champion in his path. Build Rage in terrain with walls, enter the fight in Mega Form, and use Gnar R GNAR! to slam enemies into a wall.
Kled.watch: If you’re caught by Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, create distance before it pulls you in. Save Gnar E Hop to make it harder for Kled to stay in melee range. If Kled W Violent Tendencies is active, back off so you don’t get hit by the fourth attack. Before Kled’s courage bar fills after he dismounts, assess whether you can finish him off.

Malphite.watch: Malphite Q Seismic Shard steals movement speed, so do not start a trade right after it hits you, and do not stay in its range for long. Malphite E Ground Slam reduces attack speed, so wait outside its area and attack after it is used. Malphite R Unstoppable Force cannot be interrupted with crowd control, so when you cannot see him, avoid giving him an angle to engage near walls and bushes.
Malphite.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Malphite Q Seismic Shard, E Ground Slam, and R Unstoppable Force.
Malphite.fight: Do not force an engage if you have been hit by Malphite Q Seismic Shard or Malphite E Ground Slam is still available. At full Rage, hold your abilities until the moment to engage, then close in with Gnar E Hop and transform.
Malphite.laning: Malphite Q Seismic Shard cannot be dodged from behind minions, so do not stay in his retaliation range for long. Control how much you trade so your Rage does not fill in a bad position, and finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar wears off.
Malphite.combo: As Mini Gnar, attack in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, bouncing after landing on a unit → basic attack. Catch the boomerang on its return path. For a transforming all-in, use Gnar E Hop at full Rage to land as Mega Gnar, then follow with Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you can line up a wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to throw Malphite into it and stun him, then follow with Gnar W Wallop.
Malphite.escape: Once Malphite E Ground Slam is on cooldown, close in while avoiding its attack speed slow and attack, then catch Malphite with Gnar R GNAR!.
Malphite.teamfight: Spread out from allies so Malphite R Unstoppable Force does not knock up several of you, and do not push forward recklessly when you cannot see Malphite. Counterattack after Malphite R Unstoppable Force is on cooldown, and wait outside Malphite E Ground Slam's area before attacking. As Mini Gnar, build Rage from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then get an angle to a wall as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR!.

Mordekaiser.watch: Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp can pull in multiple champions and set them up for Mordekaiser Q Obliterate and passive P Darkness Rise, so don't group up in front of him. His passive P Darkness Rise aura activates after you take three hits from his abilities or basic attacks, so trade only one or two hits before backing off. When Mordekaiser R Realm of Death is ready, don't enter its range alone; avoid a duel where your allies can't help you.
Mordekaiser.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots early on. Mordekaiser's main abilities deal magic damage, and Gnar has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If you can't finish the fight during Mega Gnar's duration because of Mordekaiser W Indestructible's healing, buy Executioner's Calling early to reduce his healing.
Mordekaiser.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip away with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before entering Mordekaiser's counterattack range. Finish the trade before taking three hits from Mordekaiser and activating his passive P Darkness Rise. When your Rage is full and you have an opening to engage, close in with Gnar E Hop, transform into Mega Gnar, and finish the fight before the transformation ends.
Mordekaiser.laning: Rage builds even when you take damage, so manage your trades to avoid transforming under the enemy turret or somewhere your allies can't support you. If you don't have an opening to engage, hold your abilities even when the meter is full, and make sure you have room to retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Mordekaiser.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → land on a unit and bounce with Gnar E Hop → basic attack. Move so you can catch Gnar Q Boomerang Throw on its return, and keep attacking the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. For an all-in, engage with Gnar E Hop while your Rage is full, transform, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a good angle on a wall, position yourself and use Gnar R GNAR! to push the enemy into it, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Mordekaiser.escape: After Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp is used, you have a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. Mordekaiser has no mobility ability, so it's hard for him to create distance once caught, but don't enter the range of Mordekaiser R Realm of Death alone while it's ready. Rage won't build for a while after Mega Gnar ends, so finish the fight and retreat before the transformation wears off.
Mordekaiser.phase: In the late game, make the most of Mega Gnar in areas with good angles to push enemies into walls.
Mordekaiser.teamfight: Before a fight, choose an area with good wall angles and position yourself so the enemy has their back to a wall. Engage as Mega Gnar, use Gnar R GNAR! to push enemies into a wall, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you're still Mini Gnar, build Rage while harassing from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, and keep your distance from allies so Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp can't pull you in together.

Olaf.watch: Olaf Q Undertow reduces Gnar's armor and slows him, setting up a chase. Move opposite the direction the axe lands to prevent Olaf from picking it up. While Olaf R Ragnarok is active, Gnar W Wallop's stun and Gnar R GNAR!'s crowd control won't work, so create distance and use them after it ends.
Olaf.build: Build armor first to defend against Olaf Q Undertow and his basic attacks. You can't reduce the true damage from Olaf E Reckless Swing with resistances, so build health as well. Reducing attack speed can also help lower the damage from Olaf's basic attacks.
Olaf.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass the same target with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to make use of Gnar W Hyper's bonus damage and movement speed. Don't stay close and fight for long even if Olaf's health has decreased, since his attack speed and lifesteal increase. When your Rage is full and Olaf R Ragnarok has ended, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform.
Olaf.laning: Early on, use your range advantage to chip away with basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before Olaf can reach you. Move away from where Olaf Q Undertow's axe lands to cut off his path to retrieve it. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities if you're in a bad position, and finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Olaf.combo: After Olaf R Ragnarok ends, use Gnar E Hop while your Rage is full to bounce off a unit and transform. Land as Mega Gnar and attack in this order: Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you're positioned to push him into a wall, finish with Gnar R GNAR!, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Olaf.escape: You have a chance to engage when Olaf Q Undertow misses and he can't retrieve the axe. Olaf has no ability to create distance on his own, so once Olaf R Ragnarok has ended, close the gap with Gnar E Hop and catch him with Gnar R GNAR!.
Olaf.phase: Olaf is strong early, so avoid giving up a kill and harass him with Gnar's range. Later on, look for an angle to engage as Mega Gnar in an area with walls.
Olaf.teamfight: Position yourself so enemies gather with their backs toward a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR! to push them into it. If Olaf R Ragnarok is active, create distance and let it run out, then apply Gnar's crowd control. If you're still Mini Gnar, build Rage while harassing from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw.

Nasus.watch: Nasus W Wither reduces both movement speed and attack speed, so don't keep trading basic attacks while affected by it. Nasus E Spirit Fire also reduces your armor within its area, so leave it. When Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, create distance and let it run out unless you clearly have the damage or numbers advantage.
Nasus.build: Build armor first to defend against Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, his main source of damage. Armor won't block the magic damage from Nasus E Spirit Fire or Nasus R Fury of the Sands, so don't rely on resistances alone; avoid the area and fights during his ultimate.
Nasus.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip away at Nasus with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before entering his counterattack range. Keep attacking the same target to make use of Gnar W Hyper's bonus damage and movement speed. If your Rage is full, hold your transformation until you have an opening to engage, then close in with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar.
Nasus.laning: From the early game, pressure Nasus as he moves in to last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, but don't push the wave all the way under his turret. Let the wave come toward your side so you can look for a jungle gank against Nasus, whose only escape is Flash. Manage your trades so Gnar's Rage doesn't trigger under the enemy turret.
Nasus.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → bounce off a unit with Gnar E Hop → basic attack, moving so you can catch the returning boomerang. To engage with a transformation, close in with Gnar E Hop while your Rage is full, land as Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a good angle on a wall, position yourself first, use Gnar R GNAR! to push him into it, and chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Nasus.escape: After Nasus W Wither is used, you have a good window to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. Nasus has no way to create distance on his own apart from Flash, so engage when your Rage and transformation position are ready. Finish the trade and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Nasus.phase: After learning Gnar R GNAR!, Gnar can find kill opportunities using walls, and his peak is in the mid game as he completes his first core item. Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks make the matchup harder over time, so in the late game choose an area with good wall angles for fights.
Nasus.teamfight: While Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, don't face him head-on; keep your distance and kite. As Mini Gnar, build Rage while harassing from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. When engaging as Mega Gnar, line up the wall first, push him into it with Gnar R GNAR!, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop.

Quinn.watch: When marked by Quinn P Harrier, back out of Quinn's basic attack range to avoid her empowered attack. Dodge Quinn Q Blinding Assault from behind your minion wave so it hits a minion first, and don't force an engage while Quinn E Vault is available.
Quinn.build: Quinn's main damage is physical, so build armor first. Investing in armor is more effective against her than investing in magic resistance.
Quinn.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks, and don't stay within Quinn's counterattack range. Once Quinn E Vault is used and your Rage is full, close the gap with Gnar E Hop, transform into Mega Gnar, and fight.
Quinn.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → bounce off a unit with Gnar E Hop → basic attack. When your Rage is full and Quinn E Vault has been used, close in with Gnar E Hop, transform, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a good angle on a wall, position yourself and use Gnar R GNAR! to push Quinn into it.
Quinn.escape: Quinn E Vault is her only mobility ability, so the moment after she uses it is your window to engage. Close the gap with Gnar E Hop / Crunch, then use Gnar R GNAR! as Mega Gnar to keep her from escaping.
Quinn.phase: In the late game, choose an area with good wall angles and maintain vision so you don't miss Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines roaming.
Quinn.teamfight: Position yourself so you can push Quinn toward a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar with Gnar R GNAR!. If Quinn approaches from the side, catch her with Gnar W Wallop or the crowd control from Gnar R GNAR!.
Quinn.laning: Back off when Quinn P Harrier marks you, and farm or trade when you’re unmarked. Stand behind the minion wave to block Quinn Q Blinding Assault. Manage your ability use when your Rage is full so you don’t transform in an unwanted position.

Ornn.watch: Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture leaves a pillar that can serve as a collision point for Ornn E Searing Charge, so stay away from pillars and walls. If Ornn W Bellows Breath’s final flame makes you Brittle, you can take extra damage and longer crowd control, so back off until the effect ends. When Ornn R Call of the Forge God begins, move sideways out of the line between the Ram and Ornn, and avoid its return path too.
Ornn.build: The reference material does not specify the first item to buy, so one cannot be identified. Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture and Ornn E Searing Charge deal physical damage, while Ornn W Bellows Breath and Ornn R Call of the Forge God deal magic damage, so consider both armor and magic resistance. Ornn W Bellows Breath deals damage based on maximum health, so be cautious about investing heavily in health alone.
Ornn.fight: As Mini Gnar, focus Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks on the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back off before entering Ornn’s counterattack range. Once Ornn E Searing Charge and Ornn R Call of the Forge God are down, use Gnar E Hop to close the gap and look for a Mega Gnar engage. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities and control your transformation timing if there is no good angle to engage.
Ornn.laning: If Ornn tries to craft an item in lane, get on him and attack to interrupt the process. Damage from minions also builds Rage, so manage your trades in positions where it is hard to use your transformation, such as under the enemy turret.
Ornn.combo: At full Rage, use Gnar E Hop on a unit to bounce toward Ornn, then land as you transform and chain Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you get an angle to throw Ornn into a wall, position yourself and finish with Gnar R GNAR!. You can also chain Gnar W Wallop after the wall stun from Gnar R GNAR! to extend your crowd control.
Ornn.escape: Do not engage just because Ornn E Searing Charge is down; check whether Ornn R Call of the Forge God is available too. In particular, before Ornn R Call of the Forge God comes back up, use the window when Ornn E Searing Charge is also down to approach with Gnar E Hop / Crunch and look for Gnar R GNAR!. Conversely, finish the fight and retreat before Gnar’s transformation ends.
Ornn.phase: Gnar can have the edge with ranged poke early, but do not stay close and fight for long. In the late game, Ornn gains items and allied Masterwork upgrades accumulate, so Gnar should choose terrain with angles for wall plays.
Ornn.teamfight: Choose a wall angle and build Rage before the fight, then engage as Mega Gnar and throw the target into a wall with Gnar R GNAR!. If you are still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage. Position yourself to avoid Ornn E Searing Charge near pillars from Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture and walls, and avoid the out-and-back path of Ornn R Call of the Forge God.

Poppy.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back off before entering Poppy’s counterattack range. Once Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge is down, use Gnar E Hop / Crunch to close the gap. If your Rage is full, hold your abilities until you have an angle to engage, then transform as you go in with Gnar E Hop.
Poppy.laning: Stay in open space to avoid the wall stun from Poppy E Heroic Charge. When Poppy P Iron Ambassador’s shield falls, step on it first to prevent her from gaining the shield. Manage your trades so Rage does not fill in an unfavorable position, and finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Poppy.combo: After Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge is down, use Gnar E Hop on a unit at full Rage to bounce in, transform, and engage. If you have a position to knock her into a wall, stun her with Gnar R GNAR!, chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop, then finish with basic attacks and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Without a wall angle, attack in this order: Gnar W Wallop stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss.
Poppy.phase: In the late game, choose terrain with angles for wall plays, and retreat while Mega Gnar has ended and Rage is not building.
Poppy.teamfight: Before the fight, choose terrain with walls and position yourself to push the target toward one. As Mini Gnar, do not force an engage; poke with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage. When engaging as Mega Gnar, confirm Poppy W Steadfast Presence has ended, then slam her into a wall with Gnar R GNAR! and chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy’s main damage from Poppy Q Hammer Shock, Poppy E Heroic Charge, and Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict. Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid relying on a large health stack alone. Don’t spend extra resources on magic resistance just to deal with Poppy.
Poppy.escape: Right after you force Poppy to use Poppy E Heroic Charge is an opportunity to close the gap with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. If Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, don’t dash in; wait for its duration to end. If Poppy charges Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict, move sideways out of its path to avoid being displaced, then look for another angle to engage.
Poppy.watch: When Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, leaping in with Gnar E Hop / Crunch will stop your dash and briefly prevent you from using movement abilities, so wait until it ends. Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if it knocks you into a wall, so don’t stand with your back to one. If you’re hit by the first part of Poppy Q Hammer Shock, walk out of the area before the second part deals damage. When you see Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict charging, move sideways out of its path.

Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault is a point-and-click stun, so you cannot dodge it; do not give him the range to use it. When Pantheon uses Q Comet Spear to poke, keep minions between you. During Pantheon E Aegis Assault, do not deal damage from the front; wait for it to end or move to the side. When you see the landing indicator for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of the landing area.
Pantheon.build: Pantheon’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid investing heavily in health alone. Pantheon has relatively high armor, so include penetration in your damage build and make use of Gnar W Hyper’s damage based on maximum health.
Pantheon.fight: As Mini Gnar, whittle Pantheon down with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks, then back off before entering Pantheon W Shield Vault’s range. Once Pantheon E Aegis Assault ends or you have his flank, keep attacking the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. At full Rage, if you have an angle to engage, close the gap with Gnar E Hop as you transform and finish the fight as Mega Gnar.
Pantheon.laning: Keep a minion between you and Pantheon Q Comet Spear to reduce its damage when it hits. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities and delay transforming if you do not have a good place to engage. Wrap up the fight and retreat before your transformation ends.
Pantheon.combo: At full Rage, approach by bouncing off a unit with Gnar E Hop; you can transform into Mega Gnar as you land. If you have a wall angle, position yourself to push the target toward the wall, stun them with Gnar R GNAR!, then extend the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. While Pantheon E Aegis Assault is blocking frontal damage, do not rush your combo; wait for it to end or move to the side.
Pantheon.escape: Once Pantheon W Shield Vault is down, look for a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop. Check that Pantheon R Grand Starfall is also unavailable before going in to reduce the chance he escapes with another movement ability. If you land Gnar R GNAR! toward a wall, the stun can prevent his escape.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon is strong in trades early, so use Gnar’s ranged poke without giving up a kill. His impact falls off later, so look for Mega Gnar fights in terrain with angles for wall plays.
Pantheon.teamfight: Before the fight, choose terrain with a wall and position yourself so the target has their back to it. Engage as Mega Gnar, push the target into the wall with Gnar R GNAR! to stun them, then follow up with Gnar W Wallop. If you are still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage. If you see the landing indicator for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, move out of its landing area.

Renekton.watch: When Renekton P Reign of Anger is over half full or just below that, respect the stun from empowered Renekton W Ruthless Predator and keep your distance. Renekton E Slice and Dice unlocks a second dash if the first one hits a unit, so do not stand in or behind a minion wave.
Renekton.fight: When Renekton's Fury bar from Renekton P Reign of Anger is empty, trade with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks. Keep hitting the same target to gain Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed, then back off before entering counterattack range. Right after Renekton uses Renekton E Slice and Dice, look for a chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop, but finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Renekton.laning: Renekton can use minions as a stepping stone to engage with Renekton E Slice and Dice, so do not stand in or behind a minion wave. Even at full Rage, hold your abilities if you do not have an angle to engage, and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Renekton.combo: If you have an angle to knock the target into a wall, stun them with Gnar R GNAR! and chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop. For a short trade as Mini Gnar, attack in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, Gnar E Hop, basic attack. Move in time with the returning path of the boomerang.
Renekton.escape: Right after Renekton has spent Renekton E Slice and Dice to disengage is your window to go in with Gnar E Hop. It is also a good time to trade back if he has just used up Renekton Q Cull the Meek and Renekton W Ruthless Predator too. Conversely, if Renekton’s Fury is around half or higher, delay your engage and respect the stun from empowered Renekton W Ruthless Predator.
Renekton.phase: In the late game, fight in terrain with angles for wall plays.
Renekton.teamfight: Choose terrain with walls ahead of the fight and position yourself so the target has their back to one. Engage as Mega Gnar, push the target into the wall with Gnar R GNAR! to stun them, then chain the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you are still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage.
Renekton.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Renekton Q Cull the Meek, Renekton W Ruthless Predator, and Renekton E Slice and Dice. However, the empowered recast of Renekton E Slice and Dice reduces your armor, so prioritize positioning where that dash can’t hit you. If Renekton’s healing from Renekton Q Cull the Meek keeps you from finishing the fight during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing.

Riven.watch: Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven E Valor chain short dashes to cover a long distance, so back away when you see the first dash. Keep your distance to avoid Riven W Ki Burst's stun. When Riven R Blade of the Exile is active, Riven's attack range increases, so retreat until it expires. Be especially wary of the finishing damage from Riven R Blade of the Exile when health has been reduced.
Riven.build: Riven's main damage is physical, so buy armor items first. If Riven gets ahead, prioritize defensive items even sooner, and build health to give yourself a better chance of surviving the finishing damage from Riven R Blade of the Exile.
Riven.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip Riven down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, and back away when you see Riven's first dash. After Riven Q Broken Wings has been used to clear minions or has been fully expended, if your Rage is full, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform as you fight. Look for a chance to interrupt Riven's remaining combo with Gnar R GNAR! right after she engages.
Riven.laning: Punish Riven when she uses Riven Q Broken Wings on minions, and don't chase too far if Riven E Valor is still available. Taking damage also builds Rage, so manage your trades to avoid an unwanted transformation under the enemy turret.
Riven.combo: When your Rage is full, engage on Riven with Gnar E Hop and transform, then chain Gnar W Wallop's stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Before using Gnar R GNAR!, position yourself so Riven will hit a wall. If you land the wall stun, extend the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop.
Riven.escape: The window before Riven Q Broken Wings comes back is your chance to engage. Once you see that Riven Q Broken Wings was used on minions or Riven E Valor is on cooldown, close the distance with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. If you have an angle toward a wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to stop Riven from escaping.
Riven.phase: In the late game, fight in areas where you have an angle to knock enemies into a wall.
Riven.teamfight: Before a fight, choose an area with a wall angle and position yourself so you can push Riven toward the wall. As Mini Gnar, build Rage from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then look for a wall stun with Gnar R GNAR! when you engage as Mega Gnar. Using Gnar R GNAR! right after Riven engages can interrupt her remaining combo.

Rumble.watch: Rumble Q Flamespitter deals damage based on your maximum health in a close-range cone, so minimize the time Rumble stays on top of you. If you're hit by the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, immediately create distance or escape with Gnar E Hop to avoid the second shot's heavy slow and magic resistance reduction. When Rumble activates Rumble W Scrap Shield, don't deal heavy damage until the shield disappears.
Rumble.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Rumble's main damage is magic, and Rumble E Electro Harpoon reduces magic resistance, so choose defensive items with magic resistance instead of building only health or armor.
Rumble.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip Rumble down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back away before Rumble Q Flamespitter can hit you for long. Focus your basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw on the same target to gain Gnar W Hyper's bonus damage and movement speed. If your Rage is full, hold your abilities until you have an opening to engage, then transform as you approach with Gnar E Hop.
Rumble.laning: Taking damage also builds Rage, so manage your trades to avoid an unwanted transformation under the enemy turret or somewhere without allied support. Rage won't build for a while after Mega Gnar ends, so finish the fight and retreat before you transform back.
Rumble.combo: For a short trade as Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → bounce off a unit with Gnar E Hop → basic attack. For an all-in at full Rage, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform, then chain Gnar W Wallop's stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you can position to push them toward a wall, stun them with Gnar R GNAR! and extend the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Rumble.escape: If you're hit by the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, you can escape with Gnar E Hop before the second shot arrives. Conversely, if Rumble W Scrap Shield has been used, its shield has disappeared, and the threat from Rumble E Electro Harpoon has passed, take advantage of Rumble having no mobility spell and engage with Gnar E Hop.
Rumble.phase: In the late game, Gnar is more valuable when fighting in areas where you have an angle for a wall stun.
Rumble.teamfight: Before a fight, choose an area where you can push enemies toward a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar and look for a wall stun with Gnar R GNAR!. If you're still Mini Gnar, harass from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build Rage. Position yourself to finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.

Sett.watch: Sett W Haymaker's shield and damage increase right after Sett has taken a lot of damage, so create distance after harassing him and wait for his Grit to fade. When dodging, move to the side of the center of its indicator to avoid the true damage. Sett E Facebreaker stuns if it catches an enemy on each side, so don't face Sett with a minion or ally between you. If Sett R The Show Stopper catches you, you'll be suppressed and can't escape with Flash, so keep your distance while his ultimate is available.
Sett.build: Build armor first against Sett's basic attacks and Sett Q Knuckle Down. You can't reduce the center's true damage from Sett W Haymaker with resistances, and Sett Q Knuckle Down deals damage based on your maximum health, so focus on dodging the center of W Haymaker rather than simply increasing health by a large amount.
Sett.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass the same target with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to make use of Gnar W Hyper's bonus damage and movement speed. When Sett walks toward you, back away before he gains movement speed. Immediately after dealing heavy damage, briefly create distance and watch for Sett W Haymaker. If your Rage is full and you have an opening, engage with Gnar E Hop, transform, and follow up with Mega Gnar's stun.
Sett.combo: For a short trade as Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → land on a unit and bounce with Gnar E Hop → basic attack. Moving in a direction that lets you catch the boomerang can greatly reduce Gnar Q Boomerang Throw's cooldown. For a transformation all-in, start at full Rage by engaging with Gnar E Hop, then chain Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle to push them into a wall, stun them with Gnar R GNAR! and extend the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop.
Sett.escape: If Sett E Facebreaker is on cooldown or you can position where it won't catch enemies on both sides, close the distance with Gnar E Hop while reducing the risk of being stunned. If your Rage is full at that point, you can transform as you engage, then catch Sett with Gnar R GNAR!.
Sett.phase: In the late game, choose areas with a wall angle to make Mega Gnar's engage more valuable.
Sett.teamfight: Before a fight, position yourself so you can drive the enemy toward a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar and push them into it with Gnar R GNAR!. Follow up on the wall stun with Gnar W Wallop to maintain crowd control. If you're still Mini Gnar, harass from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, build Rage, and wait for your chance to engage.

Singed.watch: Don't chase a low-health Singed through Singed Q Poison Trail. You can't use Gnar E Hop / Crunch on Singed W Mega Adhesive, and if Singed E Fling hits you there, you'll also be rooted, so go around areas covered by the adhesive. If Singed has his back to an ally, he can use Singed E Fling to throw you toward them, so don't stand in front of him.
Singed.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Singed's main damage is magic, and Gnar has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Singed.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then move out of retaliation range when you gain movement speed. If your Rage is full, hold your abilities until you have an opening, then engage with Gnar E Hop and transform. Finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Singed.laning: Damage from minions also builds Rage, so manage your trades to avoid transforming in a disadvantageous position, such as under the enemy turret. Don't chase along Singed Q Poison Trail.
Singed.combo: At full Rage, use Gnar E Hop to land on the enemy or a unit and bounce forward to engage, transforming into Mega Gnar. Then attack in this order: Gnar W Wallop's stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle toward a wall, position yourself to push the enemy into it and use Gnar R GNAR!.
Singed.escape: Singed has no ability that creates distance on its own, so close the distance with Gnar E Hop when Singed E Fling is on cooldown, without stepping on Singed W Mega Adhesive. If you've caught Singed as Mega Gnar, you can stun him with Gnar R GNAR! when you have a wall angle. Retreat when Mega Gnar is about to end, or just after it ends while Rage isn't building.
Singed.phase: Once Singed has his core items, he's harder to catch, so fight in areas with a wall angle in the late game.
