Singed.teamfight: Before a fight, choose an area with a wall, and if you're Mini Gnar, build Rage from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. When you engage as Mega Gnar, pin Singed down with Gnar R GNAR! aimed at a wall and attack his allies. Don't chase Singed all the way along Singed Q Poison Trail.

Shen.watch: If Shen E Shadow Dash taunts you, you'll be hit by basic attacks empowered by Shen Q Twilight Assault, so dodge the dash path and retaliate as soon as it misses. When Shen uses Shen Q Twilight Assault, also move out of the way of the Spirit Blade’s path as it returns to him. Basic attacks are negated inside Shen W Spirit's Refuge, so keep your distance and wait for its duration to end.
Shen.build: Prioritize tenacity because being held by Shen E Shadow Dash’s taunt is dangerous. Shen E Shadow Dash deals physical damage, while Shen Q Twilight Assault deals magic damage, so account for both armor and magic resistance. Shen Q Twilight Assault deals damage based on your max health, so stacking health alone offers little value.
Shen.laning: Take control early with ranged attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, and push the lane to make Shen farm. This lets you gain an advantage in the lane Shen leaves when he uses Shen R Stand United to affect another lane. Taking damage or drawing minion aggro also builds rage, so manage your trades to avoid transforming at an unwanted time under the enemy turret.
Shen.combo: After Shen E Shadow Dash misses, use this short Mini Gnar trade: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, landing on a unit to bounce → basic attack. For an all-in at full rage, use Gnar E Hop to reach Shen and transform, then stun him with Gnar W Wallop and follow with basic attacks and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a wall angle, position first, then use Gnar R GNAR! to knock Shen into the wall and continue the control with Gnar W Wallop.
Shen.escape: Shen E Shadow Dash is Shen’s only hard crowd control, so the moment it misses is your chance to engage with Gnar E Hop. If Shen R Stand United is not available, use Gnar E Hop / Crunch to close in and look for Gnar R GNAR!.
Shen.phase: In the late game, make the most of Mega Gnar in terrain with wall angles. When your transformation ends, back off to prepare for the weaker period when you can’t build rage.
Shen.teamfight: If Shen disappears or you see him channeling Shen R Stand United, alert your team immediately and assess whether you can finish the fight before he arrives. Gnar should position to drive Shen and the enemy team toward a wall, then engage in Mega form and use Gnar R GNAR!. If you’re still Mini, harass from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build rage, then finish the fight before your transformation ends.
Shen.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass Shen with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back off before entering the counterattack range of Shen E Shadow Dash. If Shen E Shadow Dash misses, close the distance with Gnar E Hop, keep attacking the same target, and trigger Gnar W Hyper. If your Rage is full, hold off on transforming and save your other abilities until the moment to engage.

TahmKench.watch: If Tahm Kench P An Acquired Taste has stacked twice, move out of range before Tahm Kench Q Tongue Lash can stun you or Tahm Kench R Devour can catch you. When you see the animation for Tahm Kench W Abyssal Dive, spread out from your allies to avoid the area knock-up. Tahm Kench E Thick Skin turns damage taken into a shield or healing, so don’t repeat trades that deal only a little damage.
TahmKench.build: Since Tahm Kench’s main damage is magic, buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads. Against Tahm Kench’s high armor, use penetration or the max-health damage from Gnar W Hyper. If his healing prevents you from settling the fight during Mega form, buy Executioner's Calling earlier.
TahmKench.fight: As Mini Gnar, harass with ranged attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, but back off as Tahm Kench P An Acquired Taste stacks build. Once Tahm Kench W Abyssal Dive is down and your rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to engage and transform, then briefly focus your damage. Finish the fight before Mega form ends.
TahmKench.laning: Catch Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and use it again to keep harassing, but manage your rage so minion damage doesn’t trigger a transformation in an unwanted position. Only commit to a fight just after transforming into Mega Gnar, and back off before the transformation ends.
TahmKench.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, landing on a unit to bounce forward → basic attack the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. At full rage, all-in by engaging with Gnar E Hop and transforming, then use Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a wall angle, throw Tahm Kench into the wall with Gnar R GNAR! and follow up with Gnar W Wallop to extend the stun.
TahmKench.escape: Once Tahm Kench W Abyssal Dive is down, it’s harder for him to engage or escape, so look to engage when Tahm Kench P An Acquired Taste has no stacks either. If your rage is full, close the gap with Gnar E Hop and transform; when you have a wall angle, catch him with Gnar R GNAR!.
TahmKench.phase: In the late game, choose terrain with walls to create an engage angle for Mega Gnar.
TahmKench.teamfight: Position so the enemy is pushed toward a wall, and look for an angle to throw them into it with Gnar R GNAR! in Mega form. If you’re Mini, don’t force an engage; harass with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build rage. Account for Tahm Kench R Devour protecting the target he’s guarding if it’s available, and focus your damage on Tahm Kench if he devours an ally.

Sion.watch: When Sion charges Sion Q Decimating Smash, use Gnar E Hop to move sideways and avoid the knock-up and stun. Sion R Unstoppable Onslaught charges in an almost straight line, so dodge sideways instead of running forward or backward. After Sion is killed, Sion P Glory in Death revives him and lets him attack quickly, so don’t keep fighting in place; create distance.
Sion.build: Build armor first against the main damage from Sion P Glory in Death, Sion Q Decimating Smash, and Sion R Unstoppable Onslaught. Sion W Soul Furnace and Sion E Roar of the Slayer deal magic damage, and E also reduces armor, so move to avoid being hit. P’s damage scales with your max health, so be careful about stacking health alone.
Sion.fight: As Mini Gnar, whittle Sion down with ranged attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then keep attacking the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. Just after Sion activates Sion W Soul Furnace, focus damage on the shield and look for a chance to break it before it explodes. When your rage is full and you have an opening to engage, use Gnar E Hop to approach and transform; finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Sion.combo: For a Mini Gnar trade, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then Gnar E Hop onto a unit to bounce forward and follow with a basic attack. At full rage, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar, then use Gnar W Wallop, a basic attack, and Gnar Q Boulder Toss in that order. Before finishing with Gnar R GNAR!, position so you can throw Sion into a wall.
Sion.escape: If you made Sion end Sion Q Decimating Smash’s charge early or dodged it to the side, close the gap if your rage and Gnar E Hop are ready. Before engaging as Mega Gnar, also check the cooldown of Gnar E Hop so you can escape after the transformation ends.
Sion.phase: In the late game, account for Sion’s increased max health and fight in terrain where Gnar can use walls.
Sion.teamfight: Before the fight, position where you can push Sion toward a wall. Engage as Mega Gnar and use Gnar R GNAR! to knock him into the wall, then continue the stun with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, harass from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build rage, then finish the fight before Mega Gnar ends.
Sion.laning: Move to meet the boomerang on its return path to catch Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. Sion gains maximum health each time he kills a unit, so push the lane to disrupt his farming or make gains in another lane.

Skarner.watch: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact dashes through terrain, and hitting a wall while grabbed stuns you, so don’t stand with your back to a wall. Skarner R Impale suppresses you and drags you along, so stay out of range.
Skarner.fight: As Mini Gnar, focus Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks on the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, and back off when you are within range of Skarner Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval’s empowered basic attacks. Once Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down and your rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to engage, transform, and fight.
Skarner.laning: Even at full rage, delay your abilities to control when you transform if you don’t have an opening to engage. Finish the fight and back off before Mega Gnar ends.
Skarner.combo: Once Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down and your rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to engage and transform, then follow with Gnar W Wallop’s stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Before using Gnar R GNAR!, position so you can push Skarner into a wall.
Skarner.escape: The moment Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down is your chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. However, if Skarner R Impale is still available, check your engage position, since he can suppress you when you get close.
Skarner.phase: In the late game, fight in terrain with wall angles. It is important to delay the point at which Skarner acquires his tank items.
Skarner.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Prioritize magic resistance against the magic damage from Skarner P Threads of Vibration, W Seismic Bastion, and R Impale. If you need to remove suppression, consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar.

Teemo.watch: Teemo Q Blinding Dart negates Gnar’s basic attacks, so if it hits, use abilities instead of basic attacks or back off. Teemo E Toxic Shot applies poison damage even with one basic attack, so stay out of range unless you’re ready to engage. Watch for Teemo P Guerrilla Warfare stealth in brush where you have no vision, and beware Teemo R Noxious Trap near objectives and in narrow paths.
Teemo.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Teemo’s main damage is magic, and Gnar has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Teemo.fight: As Mini Gnar, poke with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks, but avoid trades where you take Teemo E Toxic Shot’s poison and then back off. If Teemo Q Blinding Dart is down and your Rage is full, close the gap with Gnar E Hop, transform into Mega Gnar, and fight to the finish. While blinded, don’t insist on basic attacks; use Gnar Q Boulder Toss or Gnar W Wallop instead.
Teemo.laning: As Mini Gnar, chip away with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks, then back off before Teemo comes close enough to counterattack. Move along the boomerang's return path to catch it so you can poke again sooner. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities if there’s no opening to engage, and finish the trade and retreat before your transformation ends.
Teemo.combo: When Teemo Q Blinding Dart is down and your Rage is full, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar. If you’re positioned to push Teemo into a wall, stun him with Gnar R GNAR!, extend the stun with Gnar W Wallop, then hit Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If there’s no wall angle, lock him down first with Gnar W Wallop, then follow up with basic attacks and Gnar Q Boulder Toss.
Teemo.escape: The moment Teemo Q Blinding Dart goes down is your chance to engage using basic attacks too. Teemo W Move Quick increases his movement speed, but he has no separate escape ability, so close the gap with Gnar E Hop. If your Rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to engage and transform, then use Gnar R GNAR! to keep him from escaping.
Teemo.phase: In the late game, fight in terrain with wall angles, and keep moving so Teemo doesn’t have time to place mushrooms.
Teemo.teamfight: Use Oracle Lens to clear Teemo R Noxious Trap near objectives and in narrow passages. As Mini Gnar, build Rage from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw; when engaging as Mega Gnar, position so you can push the enemy toward a wall. Slam them into the wall with Gnar R GNAR!, then extend the stun with Gnar W Wallop.

Tryndamere.watch: When Tryndamere hits minions to build Battle Fury, his Tryndamere P Battle Fury critical strikes and Tryndamere Q Bloodlust healing become stronger, so keep your distance. Tryndamere E Spinning Slash lets him close the gap, and Tryndamere W Mocking Shout slows you when you turn your back and retreat. When Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, use Gnar W Wallop to lock him down or keep your distance until it expires instead of unloading your attacks.
Tryndamere.build: Tryndamere’s main damage is physical and based on critical strikes, so build armor first. If his healing makes it hard to finish the fight during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing.
Tryndamere.fight: As Mini Gnar, focus Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and ranged basic attacks on the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back off before entering Tryndamere’s counterattack range. When your Rage is full and Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down, engage with Gnar E Hop and transform. Finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar ends.
Tryndamere.combo: When Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down and your Rage is full, engage by bouncing off a unit with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar. Position to push him toward a wall, stun him with Gnar R GNAR!, then extend the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. Follow up with basic attacks and Gnar Q Boulder Toss, but keep your distance when Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active.
Tryndamere.escape: Right after you bait Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is your chance to close the gap with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. Once Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down, landing Gnar R GNAR! from a wall angle can stun him and prevent him from escaping again. If you’re hit by Tryndamere W Mocking Shout, it reduces your attack damage, so don’t immediately start a basic attack trade.
Tryndamere.phase: In the late game, fight in terrain with wall angles, and retreat while Mega Gnar has ended and your Rage isn’t building.
Tryndamere.teamfight: Take position near a wall first, then engage as Mega Gnar and stun Tryndamere against the wall with Gnar R GNAR! before locking him down with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke and build Rage from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. If Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, wait it out with crowd control and spacing. When he pushes a side lane, check whether his R is available and respond accordingly.
Tryndamere.laning: When Tryndamere starts hitting minions to build Fury, create some distance. If you need to dodge Tryndamere W Mocking Shout, keep facing him as you walk backward. Even with Gnar’s Rage full, if you don’t have an angle to engage, hold your abilities and delay transforming.

Trundle.watch: If you’re hit by Trundle Q Chomp, your attack damage is reduced, so keep your distance until the effect ends. Don’t fight on Trundle W Frozen Domain; back out and wait out its duration. Trundle E Pillar of Ice blocks your escape and slows you, so move to the side as soon as it appears. Keep your distance while Trundle R Subjugate is active.
Trundle.build: Build armor first to withstand Trundle Q Chomp and his basic attacks. If his healing makes it hard to win during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing. Trundle R Subjugate deals damage based on your maximum health and steals your resistances, so prioritize keeping your distance over stacking more health or resistances.
Trundle.fight: As Mini Gnar, keep hitting the same target with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then back off before entering Trundle’s counterattack range. When Trundle W Frozen Domain ends and Trundle E Pillar of Ice is down, if your Rage is full, close the gap with Gnar E Hop, transform into Mega Gnar, and finish the fight quickly. End the fight if Trundle R Subjugate is active or Mega Gnar is about to end.
Trundle.laning: Trundle heals when nearby enemy units die, so after chipping away at his health, push the lane to force him to recall or take an immediate advantage. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities and delay transforming if there’s no opening to engage.
Trundle.combo: As Mini Gnar, trade in this order: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → land on a unit with Gnar E Hop and bounce → basic attack. Move along the boomerang’s return path to catch it. If you have a wall angle, position to stun Trundle against the wall with Gnar R GNAR!.
Trundle.escape: Trundle has no ability to create distance on his own, so engage with Gnar E Hop during the window after Trundle E Pillar of Ice is down and Trundle W Frozen Domain ends. If the pillar appears, first move to the side to secure an escape route. Finish the fight and retreat before Mega Gnar’s transformation ends.
Trundle.phase: In the late game, look for team fights in terrain with wall angles, and don’t face Trundle alone in a side lane.
Trundle.teamfight: Set up to fight together near an objective, and position so the enemy gets pushed toward a wall. If you’re still Mini Gnar, build Rage from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then engage as Mega Gnar. Use Gnar R GNAR! from an angle that pushes them into a wall, extend the stun with Gnar W Wallop, and keep your distance while hit by Trundle R Subjugate.

Volibear.watch: When Volibear approaches with Volibear Q Thundering Smash active, watch out for the empowered basic attack’s stun and wait it out beyond his basic attack range. If you see the indicator for Volibear E Sky Splitter, move to the side to avoid the damage and slow. While Volibear R Stormbringer is available, watch for dives even under your turret, and use Gnar E Hop to dodge his landing zone.
Volibear.build: Build armor first to withstand the physical damage from Volibear Q Thundering Smash, W Frenzied Maul, and R Stormbringer. If Volibear W Frenzied Maul’s healing makes it hard to win during Mega Gnar’s duration, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing.
Volibear.fight: As Mini Gnar, hit the same target with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks to use Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. Poke while Volibear Q Thundering Smash is down, and when fighting as Mega Gnar, check whether Volibear R Stormbringer is down too. Finish the fight and retreat before your transformation ends.
Volibear.laning: Dodge the indicator for Volibear E Sky Splitter and poke again while Volibear Q Thundering Smash is down. Even with full Rage, hold your abilities and control when you transform if there’s no opening to engage.
Volibear.combo: If Volibear Q Thundering Smash and R Stormbringer are down and your Rage is full, close the gap with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar. After landing, follow up with the stun from Gnar W Wallop, basic attacks, and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have a wall angle, push the enemy into the wall with Gnar R GNAR! and extend the stun with Gnar W Wallop.
Volibear.escape: The window to poke is after Volibear Q Thundering Smash goes down. When engaging with Mega Gnar, look for a chance before Volibear R Stormbringer comes back up. If Volibear still has a way to move, he can chase you, so time your engages with Gnar E Hop and Gnar R GNAR! based on whether he has used it.
Volibear.phase: In the late game, choose terrain with wall angles for fights.
Volibear.teamfight: If Volibear approaches while attacking minions or monsters and builds stacks of Volibear P The Relentless Storm, don’t take the fight; wait for the stacks to fall off. As Mini Gnar, build Rage from the back with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw. As Mega Gnar, engage from a position where you can herd the enemy toward a wall, then push them into it with Gnar R GNAR!.

Urgot.watch: Urgot Q Corrosive Charge heavily slows you and makes you a target for Urgot W Purge if it hits, so decide immediately whether to dodge it with Gnar E Hop while it is flying toward you. Watch for Urgot E Disdain’s dash and stun. If Urgot R Fear Beyond Death hits you, get completely out of range before you reach the execution threshold.
Urgot.build: Build armor first because Urgot P Echoing Flames, Q Corrosive Charge, and W Purge deal most of their damage as physical damage. Urgot has high armor, so add penetration for Gnar’s physical damage and make use of Gnar W Hyper, which deals damage based on the target’s maximum health. Since Urgot P Echoing Flames scales with your maximum health, consider both resistances and total health rather than stacking health alone.
Urgot.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip him down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back out of Urgot’s short range. If Urgot approaches with W Purge active, walk away to create distance, and don’t stay near him long enough to take multiple hits from his leg cannons. Once Urgot E Disdain is down and your rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to close in, transform, and start an all-in.
Urgot.laning: Keep hitting the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, but save Gnar E Hop so you can avoid getting caught by Urgot Q Corrosive Charge in a situation where it would be hard to walk away. Even with full rage, hold your abilities if you don’t have an angle to get onto Urgot, and finish the fight before your transformation wears off.
Urgot.combo: For a short trade, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop, landing on a unit to bounce → basic attack, and move toward where you can catch the returning boomerang. If Urgot E Disdain is down and your rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to close in and transform into Mega Gnar, then follow with Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle to a wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to throw Urgot into it, then follow with Gnar W Wallop to extend the stun.
Urgot.escape: The window to engage is right after you make Urgot use E Disdain, his only mobility tool. If your rage is ready then, close the distance with Gnar E Hop and use Gnar R GNAR! to limit his chance to escape. If Urgot Q Corrosive Charge hits you, it’s hard to escape on foot, so use Gnar E Hop or E Crunch to get out.
Urgot.phase: In the late game, choose terrain with angles to a wall to get more value from Mega Gnar’s engage.
Urgot.teamfight: Before a fight, take position in terrain with angles to a wall. Engage as Mega Gnar, use Gnar R GNAR! to throw Urgot into the wall, then follow with Gnar W Wallop to extend the stun. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build rage. Urgot E Disdain stops at the first champion it hits, so stand behind your frontline to limit his engage angles, and finish the fight before your transformation wears off.

Udyr.watch: Right after Udyr activates E Blazing Stampede, watch for the stun on his first attack and save Gnar E Hop so you can use it before he gets on you. Don’t stay in an extended fight because of the empowered attacks from Udyr Q Wilding Claw and the slow and area damage from Udyr R Wingborne Storm. Udyr is immune to immobilizing effects during E Blazing Stampede’s Awakening, so use Gnar R GNAR! after it ends.
Udyr.build: If you can’t finish Udyr within Mega Gnar’s duration because Udyr W Iron Mantle heals him, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing. Prioritize armor for resistances, but account for the fact that armor alone can’t block all of Udyr R Wingborne Storm’s magic damage and both damage types from Udyr Q Wilding Claw. He also deals damage based on maximum health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone.
Udyr.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip Udyr down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw before he gets on you, and keep hitting the same target to gain Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. Press your attack once Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield is gone, but save Gnar E Hop to respond to Udyr E Blazing Stampede. When your rage is full and you have an engage angle, use Gnar E Hop to transform as you go in and finish the fight within Mega Gnar’s duration.
Udyr.laning: When Udyr is out of sight, track his path with vision on key routes and jungle entrances, and don’t push forward in lane. Even with full rage, delay using your abilities and hold your transformation if you don’t have an angle to get onto him. Position yourself to retreat before your transformation wears off.
Udyr.combo: As Mini Gnar, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, follow with basic attacks on the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper, then catch the boomerang on its return path. If Udyr E Blazing Stampede is down and your rage is full, use Gnar E Hop to bounce off a unit and transform, then follow with Gnar W Wallop → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. To finish, take an angle to a wall and use Gnar R GNAR! to push Udyr into it.
Udyr.escape: Right after you make Udyr use E Blazing Stampede is your window to close the distance with Gnar E Hop / Crunch. If you’ve already been stunned by Udyr E Blazing Stampede, trade back or escape while he can’t immediately stun the same target again. After Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s Awakening ends, use Gnar R GNAR! to prevent his escape.
Udyr.phase: In the late game, choose terrain where you can push enemies into a wall, and avoid fights right after Mega Gnar ends, when you can’t build rage.
Udyr.teamfight: Take position in terrain with angles to a wall first. Engage as Mega Gnar, use Gnar R GNAR! to push an enemy into the wall, then follow with Gnar W Wallop to extend the stun. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build rage. Rather than forcing a fight against a tanky Udyr with Udyr W Iron Mantle, deal with the weaker enemies behind him first, then fight with a numbers advantage.

Yone.watch: If Yone repeatedly uses Q Mortal Steel on minions, his tornado engage is ready, so keep your distance until the stacks disappear. After Yone E Soul Unbound takes him in, he can deal extra damage when he returns to his body, so if your health is low, get out of range before he returns. Yone R Fate Sealed pulls in enemies along its path and moves him behind the last champion hit, so don’t stand alone at the very back of your team in a teamfight.
Yone.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip him down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, then back away before entering Yone’s counterattack range. Don’t engage while Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado is ready. When your rage is full and Yone’s engage tool is down, use Gnar E Hop to close in and transform for a short all-in.
Yone.laning: While Yone is stacking Q Mortal Steel on minions, stay outside the tornado’s range. Taking damage also builds rage, so manage how much damage you trade to avoid transforming unintentionally under the enemy turret.
Yone.combo: For a Mini Gnar trade, use Gnar Q Boomerang Throw → Gnar E Hop to bounce off a unit → basic attack the same target. For an all-in at full rage, use Gnar E Hop to close in and transform, then follow with Gnar W Wallop’s stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle to a wall, use Gnar R GNAR! to push Yone into it.
Yone.escape: Engage during a window when Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado is down and he can’t use Yone E Soul Unbound or Yone R Fate Sealed. If only one mobility tool is down, he can use the others to escape, so don’t use Gnar E Hop too soon.
Yone.phase: In the late game, choose terrain where you can use walls, and fall back while you can’t build rage after Mega Gnar ends.
Yone.teamfight: If you’re Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to build rage, and line up Gnar R GNAR! toward a wall when you go in as Mega Gnar. Spread out from your allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield doesn’t grow larger. Check your position in the backline so you aren’t the last champion hit by Yone R Fate Sealed.
Yone.build: For your first purchase, prioritize attack speed reduction, since the cooldowns of Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone W Spirit Cleave decrease with attack speed. Yone deals mixed damage, so build both armor and magic resistance. Avoid investing heavily in health alone, given the max-health-based damage from Yone W Spirit Cleave.

Yorick.watch: Yorick E Mourning Mist slows, marks you, and deals damage based on your maximum health, so dodge its arc and don’t let it force a trade. If you’re trapped in Yorick W Dark Procession, hit the wall to break it or jump over it with Gnar E Hop. If the Maiden of the Mist marks you, Yorick’s basic attacks deal extra damage, so keep your distance from Yorick himself.
Yorick.build: Build armor first against Yorick Q Last Rites and the Mist Walkers’ attacks. Yorick E Mourning Mist and R Eulogy of the Isles deal magic damage based on maximum health, so don’t rely on armor or health alone to counter them. If you can’t finish Yorick within Mega Gnar’s duration because of the healing from Yorick Q Last Rites, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce his healing.
Yorick.fight: As Mini Gnar, chip Yorick down with ranged basic attacks and Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, and keep hitting the same target to make use of Gnar W Hyper’s bonus damage and movement speed. Dodge Yorick E Mourning Mist, then step forward to trade. If your rage is full, trigger your transformation as you engage with Gnar E Hop, and finish the fight before Mega Gnar wears off.
Yorick.combo: At full rage, use Gnar E Hop to land on Yorick or a unit and bounce toward him, transforming along the way so you land as Mega Gnar. Follow with Gnar W Wallop to stun him, then land basic attacks and Gnar Q Boulder Toss. Position yourself first so you can finish with Gnar R GNAR! toward a wall.
Yorick.escape: Dodge Yorick E Mourning Mist and go in once Yorick W Dark Procession is down. Yorick has no ability to create distance on his own, so close in with Gnar E Hop and, if you have an angle to a wall, lock him down with Gnar R GNAR!.
Yorick.phase: In the late game, make the most of Mega Gnar in terrain with angles to a wall.
Yorick.teamfight: Before a fight, position yourself so the enemy is pushed toward the side backed by a wall. Engage as Mega Gnar, use Gnar R GNAR! toward the wall, then follow up on stunned enemies with Gnar W Wallop to maintain crowd control. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and build rage.
Yorick.laning: Don’t start a fight where many graves have accumulated near Yorick. Push the wave so your minions die under Yorick’s turret. Even with full Rage, manage your ability use so you don’t waste your transformation under the enemy turret.

Yasuo.watch: Yasuo Q Steel Tempest has a narrow hitbox, so dodge to the side as he approaches instead of only backing away. After Yasuo hits Steel Tempest twice, watch for the next tornado’s knock-up and look to engage just after he throws it. Yasuo W Wind Wall can block Gnar Q Boomerang Throw, so go around the wall or save Q until it disappears.
Yasuo.build: Build armor first to counter the main damage from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest and Yasuo R Last Breath. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, but armor is still the resistance to prioritize. Attack speed reduction is also an option; it slows both Yasuo’s basic attacks and his tornado cycle.
Yasuo.fight: As Mini Gnar, first break Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw and basic attacks, then keep hitting the same target to trigger Gnar W Hyper. Look to trade when Yasuo Q Steel Tempest’s tornado is down. If your Rage is full, close in with Gnar E Hop and transform into Mega Gnar. Finish the fight and back off before Mega Gnar wears off.
Yasuo.laning: Keep the wave thin and toward your side of the lane to reduce the number of minions Yasuo can dash through with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade. Manage your Rage and ability timing so you don’t transform under the enemy turret or where your team can’t support you.
Yasuo.combo: If your Rage is full and Yasuo Q Steel Tempest’s tornado is down, use Gnar E Hop to bounce off a unit as you close in and transform into Mega Gnar. After landing, chain Gnar W Wallop stun → basic attack → Gnar Q Boulder Toss. If you have an angle on a wall, position to push Yasuo toward it and finish with Gnar R GNAR!.
Yasuo.teamfight: Position so Yasuo is pushed toward a wall, then engage as Mega Gnar and drive him into it with Gnar R GNAR!. If the stun lands, extend the crowd control with Gnar W Wallop. If you’re still Mini Gnar, poke from behind with Gnar Q Boomerang Throw to build Rage before engaging.
Yasuo.escape: Look to engage right after Yasuo throws the tornado from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest, when the threat of being knocked up is reduced for a while. Even before Yasuo R Last Breath comes back up, you have a chance to close the distance with Gnar E Hop / Crunch and lock him down with Gnar R GNAR!. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade is a short-cooldown mobility ability, so don’t assume you can safely engage just because he used it once.
Yasuo.phase: In the late game, choose terrain that gives you an angle to pin enemies against a wall.
